To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
consumers experience aesthetic products as more rewarding than non-aesthetic products.

(1) aesthetic package design is a significant driver of consumer choices, (2) it increases the activation in brain regions associated with reward processing, and (3) it is positively related to a paper-and-pencil self-report measure of affective involvement with the product.

aesthetic package design is associated with a) slower consumer decision making and b) increased neural activation in reward-related brain regions, such as the nucleus accumben and ventromedial cortex.

the question of how package designs affect consumers' product experiences and choice behavior.
how consumers experience aesthetic products.
how consumers experience and respond to aesthetic product experiences.

aesthetic product experience has an impact on the brain and behavior.
aesthetic product experiences can be investigated by using behavioral, neuroscientific, and psychometric approaches.
the results suggest that aesthetic package design is a powerful tool to enhance consumer experiences and increase product value, but only if the design is in accordance with consumer preferences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aesthetic package design can have a significant impact on consumers' product choice behavior.
aesthetic package design has an important impact on consumers, and that it is possible to measure this impact with behavioral and neuroimaging methods.
aesthetic experiences of package design are driven by reward value and that these experiences are associated with affective product involvement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aesthetics is not a mere hedonic preference, but rather a reward-driven process that is linked to the brain's reward system and the nucleus accumben.
the aesthetic design of packages can be a powerful tool for product managers to create a positive product experience for consumers.
aesthetic experiences are not only about the visual appeal of a product, but they also have a behavioral and neural component.
